title: The Radioactive Ore That Could Break China’s Grip on Rare Earths
gist: Monazite, a thorium-bearing ore found in heavy mineral sands, is the best hope for non-Chinese rare-earth supply, but thorium regulation, project failures such as Saskatchewan's, speculation and pump-and-dump dynamics, and China's export leverage make the path hard.

insights.claim: Chinese firms control roughly 90 percent of the markets for rare-earth oxides and metals, which feed permanent magnets in EVs, robots, drones and ballistic-missile submarines.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Rare-earth dependency is a core industrial and defense vulnerability.
insights.locator: The global campaigns to break China's dominance

insights.claim: Monazite is the most important rare-earth ore because heavy mineral sands are cheap to mine by dredging, need no crushing, can be concentrated on site by magnetic or gravity methods, and monazite contains 60 to 62 percent rare earths by weight.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Favors miners with mineral-sands assets in Australia, India, Brazil, Madagascar, Mozambique and South Africa.
insights.locator: Collecting the ore simply involves dredging

insights.claim: Chinese-controlled Bayan Obo is the source of roughly 40 percent of all rare-earth ore mined globally, and China imported more than 70,000 tonnes of ore last year via only four ports because monazite is Class 7 Dangerous Cargo.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Port and cargo-classification constraints are a chokepoint in China's ore imports.
insights.locator: Most of China's domestically mined monazite

insights.claim: Heavy mineral sands tend to contain a lot of thorium, and because there is no market for it, stored thorium without a planned use is treated as nuclear waste under NRC and IAEA rules, which makes handling a long-term liability.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Thorium rules, not geology, may be the binding constraint on ex-China supply.
insights.locator: The problem is they tend to have a lot of thorium

insights.claim: James Kennedy argues that rationalizing thorium regulation would end the US rare-earth crisis by turning rare earths into a byproduct of other mining.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Regulatory change on thorium would be a catalyst for ex-China rare-earth projects.
insights.quote: You rationalize the regulations around thorium and you will end the rare-earth crisis in the U.S.

insights.claim: Scaling monazite would produce more thorium than lined tailings ponds could economically hold, and the main large-scale use is nuclear power; the only operating thorium power reactor is a 2-megawatt molten-salt reactor in China running since 2023.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: China leads in the thorium reactor technology that could absorb the waste stream.
insights.locator: Kennedy said that if monazite ore

insights.claim: Mitsubishi Chemical's Malaysian yttrium plant (1979 to 1992) left radioactive waste cleanup costing about $100 million over two decades, a precedent that still haunts the industry where Lynas now runs the world's largest rare-earth processing facility.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Environmental and social-license risk remains for monazite processing in Malaysia.
insights.locator: In 1979, a subsidiary of Mitsubishi Chemical

insights.claim: Energy Fuels is the only US entity licensed to legally process monazite for rare earths, has spent over $200 million on monazite assets in Madagascar and Brazil, plans a $410 million second phase, and got a $725 million conditional loan commitment from the Trump administration in June.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Energy Fuels is the clearest US monazite play, supported by government financing.
insights.locator: A prime example of Kennedy's vision

insights.claim: The Saskatchewan Research Council plant missed its target of 40 tonnes of rare earths per month by end-2024 and 400 tonnes per year in early 2025, now targets late 2027, and will cost over 216 million CAD.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Government-built rare-earth processing has execution risk; discount timelines.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, though, a government project in Saskatchewan

insights.claim: Other monazite projects include Iluka Resources, Tronox, Hastings Technology Metals, Steenkampskraal, Astron, Sovereign Metals and Mkango, while Lynas is expanding monazite mining at Mount Weld.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Universe of ex-China monazite names to monitor.

insights.claim: The rare-earth industry is rife with pump-and-dump speculators, and the Trump administration's $1.6 billion investment for a 10 percent stake in USA Rare Earth funds Round Top in Texas, where no mine exists and may never exist; its equity raise was handled by Cantor Fitzgerald, run by the sons of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Treat government-backed rare-earth equities with caution; conflicts of interest and speculative projects.
insights.quote: The rare-earth mining business is the Afghanistan of mining
insights.locator: Consider the Trump administration's decision to invest

insights.claim: The Trump administration won no significant rare-earth concessions from Xi at either US-China summit this year, and CSIS argues China is highly likely to cut off rare earth exports to the US and allies in an Indo-Pacific escalation.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Export-cutoff risk makes independent supply chains a defense priority.
insights.quote: China is highly likely to cut off rare earth exports
insights.locator: At both U.S.-China summits this year

insights.claim: China is stepping up acquisition of rare-earth assets abroad, partly to replace lost Mountain Pass concentrate after the US invested $400 million in 2025, and possibly to lock up deposits from non-Chinese developers.
insights.speaker: Glenn Zorpette
insights.so_what: Chinese offshore asset grabs may crowd out Western developers.
